QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_63

question.text: In the E-Diksha case, 88% of participants started saving in banks rather than chit funds or non-formal sources. The SIA's BEST MoV is:

answer.text: Self-report survey + partner-bank account data (new account flag, small-value deposits pattern) + chit-fund declining enrolment in project areas + sub-sample passbook examination

explanation.text: The Logic: Multi-source triangulation: self-report (subject), bank data (administrative), chit-fund decline (proxy), passbook examination (primary document). This layered approach is SAS-1300 evidence-gold. The Trap: Options A, C, B are single-source or narrative. Cross-Exam Context: Bank-data triangulation overlaps XXIV AML (KYC-transaction pattern) and V-A (MF Distributor — SIP uptake evidence). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Partner with 1-2 named banks for the evidence-share MoU before the engagement. Bank cooperation is the single biggest bottleneck in SAS-1300 assessments.
